val_replay_deviation.statement: The frozen coarse/fine VAL metrics are stochastic by construction: MambaPlace applies T.FixedPoints(256) with PyG's default replace=True, i.e. np.random.choice with replacement on the global NumPy RNG for every object point cloud, on every eval call. The metrics recorded in the training log are one draw; any replay is another. Exact bit-reproduction is impossible (no RNG state was saved), so the gate is agreement within the measured draw band.

detail.coarse_R1: recorded 0.168 is +1.4pp above the 5-draw band (z 2.46); the TRAIN replay vs the logged TRAIN R@1/R@5 differs by -0.55pp/+1.52pp in the same draw process, so a ~2pp R@1 swing at 2000 queries is of the observed order
detail.close_R1: recorded 0.404 is +2.6pp above the band (z 7.5); not explained by the 5-draw sd, registered as unresolved rather than reconciled. It does not affect downstream pairing: every method shares this one export, so all comparisons are paired on identical candidates/positions/encodings
detail.fine_offset: recorded 0.081 vs replays 0.0805-0.0808 (z 2.36), i.e. 0.0005 apart - reproduced to log precision

val_replay_deviation.consequence: The exported VAL instantiation is marginally HARDER than the logged draw (R@1 14.65 vs 16.8) and is used as-is. No backbone retraining, no re-selection, no threshold tuning on VAL.
